r3-evidence.title: Required evidence
r3-evidence.imperative: Is the required evidence present and does it actually demonstrate the behavior? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r3-evidence.finding: Evidence reproduces and is honestly calibrated. Criterion 7 (diagnostics reproduce): re-ran pytest -q -s -> BYTE-IDENTICAL to pasted evidence (recovery 94.4% PASS, separability 31.9% FAIL, median|corr| 0.835, per-regime table + histogram all match; determinism from fixed BASE_SEED=663). Criterion 2 (SNR realism) INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED by fitting real 2023 FP2 sessions myself: field-pooled residual RMS = 12.2-14.5s across Spain/Canada/Saudi/Netherlands/Vegas (implementer claimed ~14-17s). Harness low-SNR tier uses noise_sigma=11.0 (~11s residual) which is if anything marginally EASIER than real -> the harness UNDERSTATES the real problem, not overstates it. Real physical rubber-evolution amplitude ~1.5s under ~13s residual => real SNR ~0.11-0.13, landing on the harness low band (0.136). My real fits also reproduced g4's degeneracy (Netherlands asymptote 8040s, Vegas -7870s, |corr|~0.73-0.77) confirming the big fitted asymptotes are aliasing, not genuine amplitude. DECISIVE: separability FAILS even at the cleanest high-SNR/high-bend tier (median|corr| 0.939, 33% clear 0.8), so the finding is robust to the exact SNR calibration. Criterion 4 (recovery passes only via sigma-widening) VERIFIED from JSON: low-SNR replicates carry huge asy_sigma (e.g. 1e7-1e8) -> 2-sigma interval trivially covers -> covAsy 100%; the ONE confident regime highSNR/modBend drops to recovery 66.7% (covAsy 66.7%) because tight sigmas let aliasing bias escape. So 'recovery PASSES' means 'error bars honestly wide', NOT 'estimates accurate' -- a materially important qualification, correctly flagged.
